question: Which is the first element on the periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen** is the first element on the periodic table.
 
• It has the atomic number **1** and is represented by the symbol **H**.
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant chemical element, constituting roughly 75% of the universe's elemental mass.
 
• In its most common isotope, hydrogen has one proton and no neutrons.
 
• It is a non-metal and is typically found as a diatomic gas (H₂) under standard conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hydrogen plays a crucial role in the universe's chemistry, being a primary building block of stars through the process of nuclear fusion.
 
• On Earth, hydrogen is found in water (H₂O) and organic compounds, making it essential for life.
 
• Hydrogen is also used in various industrial applications, including refining petroleum, producing ammonia for fertilizers, and as a potential clean fuel source.
 
• In the periodic table, elements are arranged based on their atomic number, electron configurations, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table was first created by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, and it has been expanded and refined over time.
